questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Panchayati Raj: Self-Government in Villages' refers to.
questions.a: Panchayati Raj is a system of local self-government in rural India: villagers manage their own affairs through panchayats at village, block and district levels, bringing governance close to the people.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Panchayati Raj: Self-Government in Villages'.
questions.a: Self-government means villagers decide local matters themselves instead of running to the state or national capital.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Panchayati Raj: Self-Government in Villages', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: panchayati raj = village + block + district levels

concepts.title: The Gram Sabha: Assembly of All Adults

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Gram Sabha: Assembly of All Adults' refers to.
questions.a: The gram sabha is the general body of all registered adult villagers; it meets to discuss village needs, approve plans and budgets, and hold the elected panchayat answerable.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Gram Sabha: Assembly of All Adults'.
questions.a: Direct democracy lives in the gram sabha: every adult has a seat and a voice before the elected members act.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Gram Sabha: Assembly of All Adults' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: The Gram Panchayat and Its Members

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Gram Panchayat and Its Members' refers to.
questions.a: Villagers elect ward members and a sarpanch to form the gram panchayat, which carries out the gram sabha's decisions, maintains water, roads and records, and levies small local taxes for village work.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Gram Panchayat and Its Members'.
questions.a: Elected representatives do the day-to-day work, but they answer to the gram sabha that chose them.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Gram Panchayat and Its Members' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Lakshmanpur: A Village Case Study' refers to.
questions.a: Lakshmanpur, a village of about 200 houses in the Himalayan foothills, shows local government at work: farmers' needs for water, roads and a school, disputes and resources, all settled through the panchayat system.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Lakshmanpur: A Village Case Study'.
questions.a: A concrete village turns civics into life: every need, from a broken road to a stolen crop, reaches the panchayat first.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Lakshmanpur: A Village Case Study' taught, and from which source text?
